title: Descent of framework coefficient-compatible exact functors and transformations
statement:
Fix the global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For each finite coefficient field $E\subset\Omega$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], use the framework raw rationalized categories $\mathcal C_E(W)=D^b_c(W,E)$ for $W=S,T$, with transition functors $T^W_{L/E}$ defined by completed integral scalar extension followed by rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Use their canonical unit maps $u^W_E:T^W_{E/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$, scalar associators $a^W_{M,L,E}:T^W_{M/L}T^W_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}T^W_{M/E}$ [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition], exact shift comparisons, and the framework common-stage categories $\mathcal C_\Omega(W)$ of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Exact means an additive functor with its specified shift comparison carrying distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category].

Suppose for every $E$ an exact $E$-linear functor $\Phi_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_E(S)$ is given, and for every $E\subset L$ a natural isomorphism
$$\beta_{L/E}:T^S_{L/E}\Phi_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_LT^T_{L/E}.$$
Assume it commutes with the composite shift comparisons, satisfies $\Phi_E(u^T_E)\circ\beta_{E/E}=u^S_E\Phi_E$, and, for every $E\subset L\subset M$ and $K\in\mathcal C_E(T)$, satisfies
$$\beta_{M/E,K}\circ a^S_{M,L,E,\Phi_EK}
=\Phi_M(a^T_{M,L,E,K})\circ\beta_{M/L,T^T_{L/E}K}\circ T^S_{M/L}(\beta_{L/E,K}).$$
Then there is an exact $\Omega$-linear functor $\Phi_\Omega:\mathcal C_\Omega(T)\to\mathcal C_\Omega(S)$ with object map $(E,K)\mapsto(E,\Phi_EK)$. For an arrow represented over $L\supset E,E'$ by $v:T^T_{L/E}K\to T^T_{L/E'}K'$, its image is represented over $L$ by
$$\beta_{L/E',K'}^{-1}\circ\Phi_L(v)\circ\beta_{L/E,K}.$$
This formula is independent of the common field and representative. Its shift comparison at $(E,K)$ is represented by that of $\Phi_E$, using the unit maps for source and target.

If a second family $\Psi_E$ with comparisons $\gamma_{L/E}$ satisfies these hypotheses and natural transformations $\tau_E:\Phi_E\to\Psi_E$ satisfy
$$\gamma_{L/E,K}\circ T^S_{L/E}(\tau_{E,K})
=\tau_{L,T^T_{L/E}K}\circ\beta_{L/E,K},$$
then they descend to a natural transformation $\tau_\Omega:\Phi_\Omega\to\Psi_\Omega$, whose component at $(E,K)$ is the class of $\tau_{E,K}$ under the unit identifications at stage $E$. Shift compatibility, invertibility, identities, vertical composition and equations between such transformations are preserved. The construction also respects composition of families: for any third scheme $V$ and family $\Xi_E:\mathcal C_E(S)\to\mathcal C_E(V)$ satisfying the analogous hypotheses, the scalar comparison of $\Xi_E\Phi_E$ is the composite of the two whiskered comparisons, and the resulting descended functor and comparisons identify with $\Xi_\Omega\Phi_\Omega$.

Agent-extracted comparison/descent interface; the blueprint does not state this auxiliary lemma separately.

proof.text: Write $A=(E,K)$ and $B=(F,H)$. For a common field $L$ write $A_L^T=T^T_{L/E}K$ and $A_L^S=T^S_{L/E}\Phi_EK$, with $a_A^T=a^T_{M,L,E,K}$ and $a_A^S=a^S_{M,L,E,\Phi_EK}$ when $L\subset M$; use the corresponding notation for $B$. The framework definition makes transport of $v:A_L^T\to B_L^T$ the map $v_M=a_B^T T^T_{M/L}(v)(a_A^T)^{-1}$. Equality of classes means equality after such transport, and sums and composites are calculated at a common field. Composita supply every common field needed below. The stage inclusion $j_E^W$ sends $f:K\to H$ to the class represented at $E$ by $(u^W_{E,H})^{-1}f u^W_{E,K}$. In particular units are isomorphisms throughout, not literal equalities of functors.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text:
For $v:A_L^T\to B_L^T$ put $Q_L(v)=\beta_{L/F,H}^{-1}\Phi_L(v)\beta_{L/E,K}$. We check transport explicitly. Abbreviate $b_A=\beta_{L/E,K}$, $b'_A=\beta_{M/E,K}$ and $d_A=\beta_{M/L,A_L^T}$, and likewise for $B$. The assumed tower equation gives $b'_A a_A^S=\Phi_M(a_A^T)d_A T^S_{M/L}(b_A)$. Thus, using the inverse of its $B$ version and then naturality of $\beta_{M/L}$,
$$\begin{aligned}
Q_M(v_M)&=a_B^S T^S_{M/L}(b_B)^{-1}d_B^{-1}\Phi_M(T^T_{M/L}v)d_A T^S_{M/L}(b_A)(a_A^S)^{-1}\\
&=a_B^S T^S_{M/L}(b_B^{-1}\Phi_L(v)b_A)(a_A^S)^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
This is precisely the transport of $Q_L(v)$. Only the given tower equation, naturality and cancellation of inverse isomorphisms enter this calculation.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text: If two representatives become equal over $M$, their images become equal over $M$ by step 2. Hence $[L,v]\mapsto[L,Q_L(v)]$ is a well-defined map on each Hom set, with the prescribed object function. At any common field, $Q_L(1)=1$ and $Q_L(wv)=Q_L(w)Q_L(v)$: expand the two right-hand factors and cancel the adjacent $\beta\beta^{-1}$. Also $Q_L(v+w)=Q_L(v)+Q_L(w)$ and $Q_L(0)=0$, by additivity of $\Phi_L$ and bilinearity of composition. Since identity, addition and composition in the framework category have these representatives, this defines the required additive functor $\Phi_\Omega$.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text: Here is also the scalar action and its compatibility. For $\lambda\in\Omega$ and $[L,v]$, choose a finite $M\supset L$ containing $\lambda$, possible since $\Omega$ is the union of its finite subextensions, and set $\lambda[L,v]=[M,\lambda v_M]$. Enlarging $M$ does not change this class: scalar extension is linear over the smaller coefficient field, by its rationalized morphism formula, and the associators commute with scalar multiplication since they are morphisms in the coefficient-linear category. The same argument handles another representative. The module laws and bilinearity follow by calculating the finitely many scalars and maps at one field. Since $\Phi_M$ is $M$-linear, $Q_M(\lambda v_M)=\lambda Q_M(v_M)$. Thus $\Phi_\Omega$ is $\Omega$-linear.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text:
For an $E$-stage map $f:K\to H$, the unit condition gives
$$\beta_{E/E,H}^{-1}\Phi_E((u^T_{E,H})^{-1}f u^T_{E,K})\beta_{E/E,K}
=(u^S_{E,\Phi_EH})^{-1}\Phi_E(f)u^S_{E,\Phi_EK}.$$
Consequently $\Phi_\Omega j_E^T=j_E^S\Phi_E$ on objects and arrows with the specified units. Write $\phi_{E,K}:\Phi_E(K[1])\to\Phi_E(K)[1]$ for its shift comparison. Define $c_{(E,K)}=j_E^S(\phi_{E,K})$. It is invertible, with inverse $j_E^S(\phi_{E,K}^{-1})$, and is exactly the component specified in the item.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text:
We verify naturality of $c$ on a general representative, not only on $E$-stage arrows. Let $\sigma_A^T:T^T_{L/E}(K[1])\to(T^T_{L/E}K)[1]$ be the transition shift comparison and set $h_A=\sigma^S_{L/E,\Phi_EK}T^S_{L/E}(\phi_{E,K})$; use analogous notation for $B$. Shift compatibility of $\beta$ is the equality
$$\beta_{L/E,K}[1]h_A=\phi_{L,A_L^T}\Phi_L(\sigma_A^T)\beta_{L/E,K[1]}.$$
A representative for $[L,v][1]$ is $v^+=(\sigma_B^T)^{-1}v[1]\sigma_A^T$. Substituting this and the displayed equality for $A,B$ into $h_BQ_L(v^+)$, naturality $\phi_{L,B_L^T}\Phi_L(v[1])=\Phi_L(v)[1]\phi_{L,A_L^T}$ cancels the middle factors and gives
$$h_BQ_L(v^+)=Q_L(v)[1]h_A.$$
After multiplying by $(\sigma^S_{L/F,\Phi_FH})^{-1}$ this is precisely $c_B\Phi_\Omega([L,v][1])=\Phi_\Omega([L,v])[1]c_A$, with the pair-category shift comparisons inserted. Therefore $c$ is a natural shift isomorphism.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text: A distinguished framework triangle is isomorphic to the image under $j_L^T$ of a distinguished triangle at one finite field $L$. By steps 5 and 6 its image under $(\Phi_\Omega,c)$ is isomorphic, as a triangle including the third arrow to the shifted first vertex, to $j_L^S$ of the triangle obtained by applying $(\Phi_L,\phi_L)$. The latter finite triangle is distinguished by the assumed exactness of $\Phi_L$; its image under $j_L^S$ is distinguished by the definition of the common-stage distinguished triangles. Distinguished triangles are closed under isomorphism. With the additivity already checked, this proves exactness with the specified shift comparison.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text:
Define $(\tau_\Omega)_{(E,K)}=j_E^S(\tau_{E,K})$, so its $E$-representative is $(u^S_{E,\Psi_EK})^{-1}\tau_{E,K}u^S_{E,\Phi_EK}$. At a larger field $L$ this component is represented, using the identity-extension compatibility of the associators and naturality of the units, by $t_A=T^S_{L/E}(\tau_{E,K})$. The assumed scalar square says explicitly
$$t_A=\gamma_{L/E,K}^{-1}\tau_{L,T^T_{L/E}K}\beta_{L/E,K}.$$
For $v:A_L^T\to B_L^T$, substitute this expression for $t_A,t_B$; naturality of $\tau_L$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
t_BQ_L^\Phi(v)&=\gamma_B^{-1}\tau_{L,B_L^T}\Phi_L(v)\beta_A\\
&=\gamma_B^{-1}\Psi_L(v)\tau_{L,A_L^T}\beta_A
=Q_L^\Psi(v)t_A.
\end{aligned}$$
Taking classes proves naturality on every arrow.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text: Identities and vertical composites of compatible transformations remain compatible: in the scalar square for a composite, substitute the first scalar square and then the second, giving $(\upsilon_L\tau_L)\beta=\delta\,T^S(\upsilon_E\tau_E)$. Their descended components are $j_E(1)=1$ and $j_E(\upsilon_E\tau_E)=j_E(\upsilon_E)j_E(\tau_E)$. Any equation between compatible transformations therefore holds at each pair object after descent. If $\tau_E$ is invertible, rearranging $\gamma T^S(\tau_E)=\tau_L\beta$ gives $\beta T^S(\tau_E^{-1})=\tau_L^{-1}\gamma$; its inverse family is compatible and descends to the inverse by the composite calculation. If the $\tau_E$ commute with shifts, apply $j_E$ to $\psi_{E,K}\tau_{E,K[1]}=\tau_{E,K}[1]\phi_{E,K}$ and use step 5: this is exactly the descended shift square at $(E,K)$. Here $j_E(f)[1]=j_E(f[1])$ for every $E$-stage map $f:K\to H$: the shift of $j_E(f)$ is represented at $E$ by $\sigma_{E/E,H}^{-1}\bigl((u_{E,H})^{-1}fu_{E,K}\bigr)[1]\sigma_{E/E,K}$, and $\mu_K=u_{E,K}[1]\,\sigma_{E/E,K}\,(u_{E,K[1]})^{-1}$ is a composite of natural isomorphisms, hence a natural automorphism of $[1]$, so this representative is $(u_{E,H[1]})^{-1}\mu_H^{-1}f[1]\mu_Ku_{E,K[1]}=(u_{E,H[1]})^{-1}f[1]u_{E,K[1]}$.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text:
For the third family write $\xi_{L/E}:T^V_{L/E}\Xi_E\to\Xi_LT^S_{L/E}$ and set
$$\delta_{L/E,K}=\Xi_L(\beta_{L/E,K})\xi_{L/E,\Phi_EK}.$$
The unit equation follows by substituting first that of $\xi$ and then that of $\beta$. For the shift square put $h^{\Xi\Phi}_A=\sigma^V_{L/E,\Xi_E\Phi_EK}T^V_{L/E}(\chi_{E,\Phi_EK}\Xi_E(\phi_{E,K}))$, $\chi$ the shift comparison of $\Xi$. Apply the shift square of $\xi$ at $\Phi_EK$, naturality of $\xi_{L/E}$ on $\phi_{E,K}$, naturality of $\chi_L$ on $\beta_{L/E,K}$, and the shift square of $\beta$ (step 6):
$$\delta_{L/E,K}[1]h^{\Xi\Phi}_A=\chi_{L,\Phi_LA_L^T}\Xi_L(\beta_{L/E,K}[1]h_A)\xi_{L/E,\Phi_E(K[1])}=\chi_{L,\Phi_LA_L^T}\Xi_L(\phi_{L,A_L^T})\,\Xi_L\Phi_L(\sigma^T_A)\,\delta_{L/E,K[1]},$$
the shift square of $\delta$ for the composite shift comparisons $\chi\,\Xi(\phi)$. To check the tower equation, the needed interchange is exactly naturality of $\xi_{M/L}$ on the arrow $\beta_{L/E,K}$:
$$\Xi_M(T^S_{M/L}\beta_{L/E,K})\xi_{M/L,T^S_{L/E}\Phi_EK}
=\xi_{M/L,\Phi_LT^T_{L/E}K}T^V_{M/L}(\Xi_L\beta_{L/E,K}).$$
Expand $\delta_{M/E}a^V$; replace $\beta_{M/E}a^S$ and $\xi_{M/E}a^V$ by their tower equations, and use this displayed interchange. The resulting expression is
$$\Xi_M\Phi_M(a^T_{M,L,E,K})\delta_{M/L,T^T_{L/E}K}T^V_{M/L}(\delta_{L/E,K}),$$
which is the required tower equation. Thus the composite family satisfies all descent hypotheses; it is exact and linear because each composite stage functor is so.

source.place: Algebraically closed coefficient paragraph: explicit common-stage descent calculation

proof.text:
The composite descended functor has the same object function as the descent of $\Xi_E\Phi_E$. Write $\xi_A=\xi_{L/E,\Phi_EK}$ and $\xi_B=\xi_{L/F,\Phi_FH}$. Its representative map is, by functoriality of $\Xi_L$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\xi_B^{-1}\Xi_L\bigl(\beta_B^{-1}\Phi_L(v)\beta_A\bigr)\xi_A
&=(\Xi_L(\beta_B)\xi_B)^{-1}\Xi_L\Phi_L(v)(\Xi_L(\beta_A)\xi_A)\\
&=\delta_B^{-1}\Xi_L\Phi_L(v)\delta_A.
\end{aligned}$$
This is the formula for descent of the composite family. The shift comparison of the composite at $(E,K)$ is represented by $\chi_{E,\Phi_EK}\Xi_E(\phi_{E,K})$, with $\chi$ the shift comparison of $\Xi_E$, exactly the composite stage shift comparison. The scalar comparisons used in this identification are $\delta$ by their definition in step 10. Components of any compatible comparison transformation identify under this equality since both are their finite-stage classes, as in steps 8 and 9. This proves the composition assertion together with all its specified comparisons.
